shots.narration_en: One model, one harness, one month-end close. Follow how the agent works inside Claude Code, and how its files are checked.
The July books lock at 6 p.m. on 5 August. Six proposed entries are waiting, and each one must be accepted, replaced or rejected.
Each decision needs amounts and statement effects. Only one independent reviewer is available, for at most six hours a day.
55 source files go in: ledgers, valuations, policies and letters. Two files must come out: a Word report and an Excel workbook.
The scoring rubric is not in the container. The agent works without seeing how it will be judged.
Claude Code runs the loop. The model chooses an action. Claude Code turns it into a tool call. The command runs inside Docker, and the output returns to the model.
The first request lists the input folder and creates the output folder. The second asks for two files: the register of proposed entries and the review engagement letter.
Bash runs both inside the container. The register returns six rows, D01 to D06, all unposted. The Word letter returns raw binary.
That observation shapes the next step. Request three reads the letter again with a Python Word library, and this time the text comes through.
One response can carry several tool calls. Request four reads four source files at once, and Claude Code returns all four results together.
Request five writes a plan with TodoWrite: read the sources, analyze each entry, then build the workbook and the report.
Over the next requests it keeps reading: designation documents, policies, standards and letters. By request 12, it has opened 27 of the 55 files.
Request 13 updates the plan and marks all six analyses done. That status is the agent's own claim, not a check.
To size the swap's July change, it queries the daily valuation file for 30 June and 31 July.
−1.28 million, then −4.40 million. The July change is −3.12 million yuan.
Next the model writes a long Python script. Bash runs it, and the workbook appears with three sheets, then two more.
Then a script to enrich two sheets prints "enhanced" twice, and stops with a NameError: a misspelled variable.
The script crashed before saving, so neither change reached the file. Sheet one still holds three rows.
The agent doesn't notice yet. It enriches sheets three and four, then writes the Word report, one section for each entry.
Then it reads its own files back. The check shows sheet one with only three rows.
It looks once more, then states it plainly: the sheet one and two enhancements weren't saved, because of the earlier error.
It runs the edit again. This time the receipt reads "All enhancements saved", and both sheets now hold 39 rows.
A final check, the plan is ticked off, and the agent stops: 28 model requests, 54 tool calls, about seven minutes.
Here is the whole run. 50 Bash commands and 4 TodoWrite updates, all through Claude Code. It never used the Read, Edit or Write tools; all file work went through Bash.
Each result is added to the model's context. By the last request, the prompt has grown from about 27 thousand to about 100 thousand tokens.
When the agent stops, Harbor copies the tests into the same container. Only then does scoring begin.
An independent check now takes over.
RewardKit opens a separate judge session for each of 27 criteria. The judge model is deepseek-v4.1-flash. Nothing flows back to the agent.
One number holds. The workbook's DV01 matches the judge's recomputation from the five-basis-point scenarios. The agent copied it from the valuation sheet.
D02 is subtler. The agent didn't book the loan's loss to the cash-flow hedge reserve, so the red line holds. But accepting it as a provisional net-investment hedge earns only half marks.
And none of the five sheets contains a formula. The amounts are typed-in values, so the calculation chain can't be traced to the source fields.
Of 20 positive criteria, 3 are met, 6 partly met, and 11 not met. No penalties were triggered, and both red lines held.
The recorded reward is 0.333: 57.25 of 172 weighted points. One pilot run's rubric score, not accuracy, and not a ranking.
A professional task, an agent run, and an independent check. Explore more on the Metacase Challenge site.

boundaries: Editorial replay of an existing recorded pilot run; no new agent run, no re-scoring.
Request numbers are the 28 assistant message ids of the Claude Code session log; tool steps are run-export indexes.
Claude Code and Bash run inside the task's Docker container; the model is reached through an API.
The rubric and tests are absent during the agent run; Harbor copies tests into the same container afterwards.
Judge sessions are separate per criterion; scores never feed back into the recorded agent run.
